summary: Tulare County, CA cooperative lookout built 1930 on Blue Ridge; lifted off the mountain in 2010, restored, and displayed at the Tulare County Fairgrounds.

facts.design: 60-foot open steel Aermotor tower with 7x7 observation cab (FFLOS); cab modified in 1960
facts.status_note: Lifted off its mountain in 2010; now displayed at the Tulare County Fairgrounds, where sources differ on whether the tower or only the cab is shown

access.note: Displayed at the Tulare County Fairgrounds; opened to visitors during the county fair in 2011 and 2024. No regular hours found in the sources read. Public access to the summit is not described.

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, Tulare Unit (CAL FIRE TUU); jointly erected with the Forest Service (FFLOS)

corrections.why: The FFLOS entry says a 60 foot tower and a December 1930 report plans 60 feet; 22.9 m (75 ft) appears in no source read. An April 1931 report says the structure rose seventy feet above its base, so a human should confirm the figure

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS dates the move to the fairgrounds to 2010. The 2010 FFLA report says the tower was lifted off the mountain in May 2010 and went to Visalia for restoration; the 2011 FFLA report says the restored tower was placed at the fairgrounds by October 2011. 2010 is the removal, 2011 the placement.

notes_for_editor: Two records describe this lookout: this one (the mountain site, coordinates match FFLOS) and us-ca-blue-ridge-lookout-site-at-tulare-county-fairgrounds (the display). Story covers both, as the brief asks. Unresolved: (1) height: FFLOS and the December 1930 report say 60 feet, the April 1931 report says 70 feet above the base; the record's 22.9 m matches neither, so the correction above is for a human to confirm. (2) Display: the 2017 Sun-Gazette says the building is on permanent display; FFLOS says only the cabin is on ground-level display. The FFLOS entry is undated apart from its assessment mark, so its date is unknown. (3) Location: 'east of Exeter' (1930) and '15 miles east of Springville' (2017). (4) FFLOS says the facilities are under the State Department of Fish and Game, while CAL FIRE is listed as administrator; not resolved. Newspaper details are from the Forest Lookouts transcriptions of the Fresno Bee, not from the papers. The fairgrounds record's claim of visitor days in 2011 and 2024 is supported by sources [4] and [5]. No current status found for the mountain house and garage, and no new photos added. Other Blue Ridge records (us-ca-blue-ridge, us-ca-blue-ridge-2) were not checked.
